column4: S4.9b: loadSoundFile never tests an mmioRead result (every `call ebx` from 0x43e8 on discards eax). The tag of the chunk loop is read into the frame local at entry esp - 0x3cc (0x43e0 / 0x43e8) and compared at 0x43ea-0x4606; a bank file that ends after a known chunk, with no 'MThd' and no other tag after it, leaves the previous tag in that local, so the same handler runs again on every pass and the loop has no exit ('ctrl' and 'chnl' allocate nothing; 'trak' / 'glbl' / 'kmap' allocate until operator new fails). The port follows the instructions (no bound). Not run: the emulated original would only stop at its instruction budget, so no key ends a file that way (every key's file ends with 'MThd' or an unknown tag). Whether real winmm's mmioRead leaves the buffer untouched at end of file is the mmio stand-in's measured model (log/c3/alt/c3fg_conform*: a short read copies only the bytes left).

S4.9b: Wave_Device::readFmtChunk (S4.9) copies the dword at its CtrlObject local's +8 into the type-3 record (0x555b), a frame dword nothing initialises (S4.9's note). Under loadSoundFile ('ctrl' chunk, 0x45ec) the port's readFmtChunk keeps its locals in audio_dev's frame block (no entry esp is passed to a nested port function), so the copied dword is that block's 0 while the emulated original copies the stack bytes at its frame (measured: arena +0x44, the original 0x00000001 in loadSoundFile@basic v1 and 0x03010302 in loadSoundFile@busy0 v0, the port 0). The keys therefore use 'ctrl' chunks of type 0, 1 and 2 only; the type-3 arm stays judged by S4.9's readFmtChunk_t3 keys, where the function is called at the top level and finds the original's stack bytes. Settled when nested port frames sit at the original's stack offsets (S4.2b's SndFrame), or by a decision that uninitialised frame bytes are not compared.

S4.9b: no file of the user's install is in loadSoundFile's format: no file under original\ starts with 'MThd' or a chunk tag ('ctrl' 'trak' 'glbl' 'chnl' 'prgm' 'kmap'), and it holds no .mid / .rmi file. Under original\Sounds 243 .wav files start with 'RIFF', one with 'FORM' (Sounds\Effects\Sheep 2.wav) and Sounds\vssver.scc with the dword 0x00011234; the install's 320 .wav files are 319 'RIFF' and that 'FORM'. Three of them (Text Box.wav, vssver.scc, Sheep 2.wav) are loaded by the key loadSoundFile@user and take the unknown-tag exit (return 8, 0x4d1f) after one 4-byte read; every other path is reached with synthetic bank files built by 9b_fixtures.js. Which caller hands loadSoundFile a name in the shipped game (create_sound 0x93e0 types 'mid' / 'rmi' as 2; the class it allocates for that type was not traced here) is not established.

S4.9b: four callees of the loadSoundFile paths have no names row and no S4 row, so the port reaches them through the dispatcher's development fallback (counted per key in the golden file as owner `unlisted`): rva 0x2e3c0 (thunk 0x132f, called at 0x422f on the 12-byte local at entry esp - 0x3d8: `+0 = 0x24`, `+4 = 0`, `+8 |= 1`, returns this; its only caller is loadSoundFile), rva 0x5f40 (Sound vtable 0x5b000 slot +0xb4: `mov eax, [ecx + 0x1b8]; ret`, called by Seq_applyTrackFlag), rva 0x2cf50 (MixBuffer vtable 0x5be84 slot 0, the deleting destructor 0x49d5 calls; it references the vtable and operator delete) and rva 0x20480 (Sound vtable slot +0x14, called at 0x4276; the keys stand it in with a recording stub). Plus the static CRT's _strrchr 0x424b0 (0x4851 / 0x4875 / 0x4b07 / 0x4b2b), strstr 0x42690 and the eh vector iterators 0x42902 / 0x4280e reached through callees (owner `-`). Production needs names and port bodies for the four (merge request section 3).

S4.9b: the module reads no file: mmioOpenA / mmioRead / mmioSeek / mmioGetInfo / mmioClose are snd_import calls through the original's IAT slots (0xb8660 / 0xb8664 / 0xb866c / 0xb8668 / 0xb8670), served in the tests by the emulator's mmio stand-in from the fixture's files and, with no host, handed to the AudioSink as `WINMM!mmioXxx` commands. The step row asks for the user's own files read through GameFiles: here 9b_replay.py reads them from original\ and gives them to the stand-in; serving mmioOpenA names from GameFiles in production is the AudioSink host's job (S4.10), not this module's.
